title: When the Verdict Turns
premise: Wendell Eastwick, a night-shift taxi dispatcher who has quietly solved three deaths the police called accidents, takes on the disappearance of Lorna Vey, a lighthouse keeper's daughter who vanished eleven years ago from the coastal town of Greyhollow. When Lorna's recovered diary continues writing entries past the date she disappeared—in handwriting that matches Wendell's own—Wendell realizes someone alive is staging the past to lure her into the one case the town swore was closed: her mother's drowning, ruled an accident when Wendell was nine. Following the diary's clues through tide charts, ferry manifests, and her mother's hidden inheritance papers, Wendell discovers the town patriarch staged both deaths to keep the harbor land in his family. In the climax at the collapsing sea wall, she forces a confession as the tide rises, choosing at last to be seen rather than safe.
about_author: Freya Eriksen grew up in a Norwegian fishing village where every family kept its secrets below the waterline, an upbringing that taught her how much a small town will forgive and what it never forgets. She now writes mysteries from a converted boathouse, drawn always to quiet observers who see more than they say.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. On a slow night shift, Wendell dispatches taxis through fog while mentally replaying the details of a hit-and-run the police closed last month—details that don't add up. She anonymously mails her third unsolicited letter of evidence to a detective. Emotional beat: the comfort and loneliness of being unseen.

chapters.title: A Diary Returned
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. A package arrives at the dispatch office containing Lorna Vey's diary, missing since her disappearance eleven years ago. Wendell reads it cover to cover and freezes: entries continue for two weeks after Lorna vanished. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Greyhollow Remembers Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Wendell visits Greyhollow's diner and bait shop, probing old neighbors about Lorna. Everyone repeats the same script—she ran off with a ferryman—and warns her to let it lie. Emotional beat: the suffocating weight of a town's agreed-upon story.

chapters.title: Handwriting Like Mine
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Comparing the post-disappearance entries to her own childhood schoolwork, Wendell confirms the impossible: the later diary pages are in her hand, though she has no memory of writing them. Emotional beat: self-doubt curdling into fear that her own mind is compromised.

chapters.title: What the Tide Took
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Flashback chapter: nine-year-old Wendell watches her mother drown off the jetty; the verdict was accident. Present-day Wendell finds the diary's final entry names the jetty and a date next week. Emotional beat: grief reopened as evidence.

chapters.title: The Detective Who Kept Her Letters
chapters.summary: POV alternating Wendell/Detective Ilsa Brandt. Brandt confronts Wendell about the anonymous letters—and reveals she kept all three because each was right. She agrees to unofficially help if Wendell stays visible this time. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, first taste of belonging.

chapters.title: Inheritance Papers in a Salt Box
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Searching her late grandmother's attic, Wendell finds deeds showing her mother co-owned the harbor flats—land the Calloway family quietly absorbed after the drowning. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed from money to motive.

chapters.title: Ferry Manifests and Missing Hours
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Cross-referencing ferry logs, Wendell proves no boat left the night Lorna vanished—the 'ran away' story is physically impossible. Someone local made her disappear. Emotional beat: cold clarity replacing doubt.

chapters.title: The Man Who Watches the Wall
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Wendell stakes out the crumbling sea wall and spots Aldous Calloway's estate manager photographing anyone who walks it. He follows her home; she loses him using taxi routes only a dispatcher knows. Emotional beat: invisibility as weapon, but also a warning shot.

chapters.title: Entries I Never Wrote
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. New diary pages appear in her mailbox, describing her own stakeout in detail. The writer knows her movements—and writes fluently in her voice. Emotional beat: hunted through her own identity.

chapters.title: Lorna's Room, Sealed Eleven Years
chapters.summary: POV Wendell with Brandt. They enter Lorna's preserved bedroom and find tide charts annotated in two hands—one adult, one child's. The child's hand is Wendell's. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past has been rehearsing her.

chapters.title: The Governess Who Stayed
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Wendell tracks down Marit, the Calloways' former governess, who taught young Wendell penmanship the summer before her mother died. Marit recognizes the forged entries instantly—and goes pale at who could have commissioned them. Emotional beat: a key turning in a long-rusted lock.

chapters.title: Aldous Calloway Opens His Door
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Wendell interviews the dying patriarch, who performs benevolence while quoting her mother's exact words from the night she died—words spoken privately. Emotional beat: polite menace; the mask slipping just enough.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Hand
chapters.summary: POV Brandt. Brandt reexamines Wendell's three solved cases and finds each victim had ties to the Calloway land deal. The pattern Wendell saw alone is now corroborated. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by dread—she was noticed all along.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The 'ferryman' Lorna allegedly ran off with is found living under another name; he admits he was paid to provide an alibi story and saw Lorna's car at the Calloway dock that night. Emotional beat: the town's story cracking open.

chapters.title: Where the Diary Was Between Years
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Tracing the diary's custody, Wendell learns it sat in the Calloway estate safe until six weeks ago—when Aldous's grandson Rowan withdrew it. Rowan has been forging entries to draw out the Eastwicks. Emotional beat: the trap has an author, and he's young and desperate.

chapters.title: Rowan's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Rowan. Rowan explains himself: his grandfather's empire is mortgaged on land whose title still legally runs through Wendell's mother's estate. He needed Wendell to sign away a claim she never knew she had—or be discredited as unstable. Emotional beat: pity entangled with fury.

chapters.title: Signature or Silence
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Rowan offers Wendell money and anonymity in exchange for signing over the harbor flats. She stalls, buying time while Brandt subpoenas the original deed. Emotional beat: the temptation of disappearing forever versus claiming what's hers.

chapters.title: What My Mother Knew
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. A hidden letter from her mother reveals she'd discovered Aldous smuggling contraband through the harbor and planned to report him; the drowning was staged. Emotional beat: her mother transformed from victim to witness.

chapters.title: The Sea Wall at High Water
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Lured by a forged diary page to the jetty at spring tide, Wendell is cornered by the estate manager as the wall begins to fail. She records his confession to both deaths on her dispatch radio, broadcasting to Brandt. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into testimony.

chapters.title: Verdicts, Old and New
chapters.summary: POV alternating Wendell/Brandt. Arrests follow; Aldous dies before charges land, but the estate falls and the harbor flats revert to Wendell. The coroner reopens her mother's case. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly, but arriving.

chapters.title: First Light, Unhidden
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Wendell walks the rebuilt jetty at dawn, hands Brandt her fourth letter in person, and accepts the town's thanks without retreating behind the dispatch desk. She keeps the diary's blank final pages—to write her own record now. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, memory honored, invisibility set down like a heavy coat.
